careerAi.title: Résumé workbench
careerAi.lede: Four model-assisted tools built on what this platform already measures: rewrite a bullet into the XYZ form, merge several versions into one, grade the document with the gaps named, and put it in front of a colleague for review.
careerAi.guarantee: Nothing on this page invents a number. Every rewrite and every merge is checked against your own document before you see it, and any suggestion asserting a figure your résumé does not contain is discarded — the original stands, and you are asked for the real number instead.
careerAi.cached: Served from the cache for these exact inputs.
careerAi.degraded: The model is unavailable, so only the measured reading is shown. {reason}

tabLede.rewrite: Accomplished [X] as measured by [Y], by doing [Z]. A deterministic pass finds the bullets missing one of those parts and the numbers your résumé already contains; the model rewrites only those lines, and anything still missing is reported honestly rather than filled in.
tabLede.merge: Keeping four résumés instead of one is what happens when a merge quietly drops the bullet that existed in only one version. This groups the near-duplicates, writes the merged wording, and lists every unique line untouched.
tabLede.grade: Two readings of the same document on the same five categories: one by counting, one by reading. Where they disagree is stated plainly instead of averaged away.
tabLede.reviews: Ask a colleague — or the model — for feedback on a résumé, and keep the conversation. The document is frozen when the question is asked, so everyone is reading the same words.

seo.title: The Ultimate Demo — Builderforce
seo.description: Follow five moves to watch one idea become a running, deployed, tested app operated by a team of humans and AI agents.
seo.ogTitle: The Ultimate Demo — build, deploy and scale in minutes

slides.title: Build, deploy and scale — in one sitting.
slides.tagline: Five moves take a single idea all the way to a running product operated by a team of humans and AI agents. Follow along.

slides.title: Zero setup. You're already in.
slides.tagline: No forms, no configuration — just an account.
steps: Create an account or log in
Land straight in your Default workspace
A Default project is already waiting for you
slides.see: You're in a working workspace in seconds — on the web or in VS Code.

slides.title: Say what you want. Watch it build.
slides.tagline: Type your idea into the "What should we build?" prompt.
steps: Type a plain-language description of your app
Land in the Builder with your prompt carried across
The AI scaffolds a complete, running app for you
slides.see: A live preview lights up with a working app — from a single sentence.

slides.title: One click live. Tested automatically.
slides.tagline: Publish, then let the agent put it through its paces.
steps: Hit Publish — your app goes live at a URL in seconds
The Agentic Tester targets the deployed app automatically
Findings come back as fix-ready tickets
slides.see: Deployed and quality-checked without ever leaving the Builder.

slides.title: Invite people. Hire agents. One team.
slides.tagline: Humans and AI agents work the same board.
steps: Invite a teammate into your workspace
Add an AI agent to your workforce
Assign work to a person or an agent — same picker
slides.see: A blended human + agent team, collaborating on one shared board.

slides.title: A lean team. An augmented workforce.
slides.tagline: A few developers direct a fleet of agents.
steps: Staff swimlanes with the right agents
Drag a ticket into a lane to auto-run an agent
Steer live runs and answer their questions as they work
slides.see: A handful of developers orchestrate a workforce of agents doing the heavy lifting.

slides.title: Idea to product to team — in minutes.
slides.tagline: You just watched one prompt become a deployed, tested app, run by a team of humans and AI agents. Now it's your turn.

gate.will_run: A run was dispatched for these tickets.
gate.no_board: The project has no board, so there is no lane for autonomy to resolve against.
gate.no_lane: No swimlane on the board matches the ticket's status, so autonomy has nothing to trigger on.
gate.terminal_lane: The ticket sits in a terminal (Done) lane, which never auto-runs.
gate.human_gate: The lane is human-gated — a person must approve it or press Run now.
gate.no_agent: The lane has no staffed agent and the owner cannot execute this stage. Staff the lane, or dispatch explicitly with Run now.
gate.managed_no_role: This board is lifecycle-managed, so every run must be attributed to a role the stage authorises — and no authorised role resolves to an agent here. Assigning an owner will not help: the assignee is the Coordinator, never the executor. Staff the lane, pin the role, or let the Coordinator resolve the stage participant.
gate.capability_mismatch: Every candidate agent lacks the skills this lane requires.
gate.already_running: A run is already live on the ticket, so no new one was dispatched.
gate.run_cap_exhausted: The last consecutive runs each either failed or finished without producing anything, so autonomy stopped re-dispatching. A human Run now overrides it.
gate.cooldown_active: The last run failed or finished with nothing to show for it, so the ticket is in its back-off window before the next autonomous attempt.
gate.not_executable: A system or coordination chore — never dispatched to an agent by design.
gate.pending_approval: An external request awaiting human acceptance in triage before any agent may touch it.
gate.unrecorded: No auto-run decision was ever recorded — autonomy never evaluated these tickets.
gate.lane_requirement_gate: The lane requires a role sign-off that is still outstanding, so the requirement gate dispatched that reviewer and suppressed the lane's normal agent until the review clears.
gate.same_lane_reentry: The run that just finished already served this lane, so the loop guard suppressed an immediate re-dispatch into it. Nothing is executing.
gate.tenant_token_limit: The workspace has used its token allowance, so autonomy is paused for every ticket it owns until the allowance resets or the plan is upgraded.
gate.cloud_run_limit: The workspace has used its monthly cloud-run allowance. Retrying will not clear this — upgrade the plan or wait for the reset. On-prem and VS Code runs stay unlimited.

cloudAgentForm.surfaceHelp: All run the full task remotely. Durable executes on-demand on a Durable Object (per step) — the default. Long-lived Cloudflare Container keeps a process running for very long, continuous tasks (falls back to Durable until Container infra is enabled). GitHub Actions runs the agent on your linked repo's own runners with a real filesystem and toolchain and a 60-minute limit — it requires the Builderforce agent workflow (.github/workflows/builderforce-agent.yml) committed to the repo, otherwise the run falls back to Durable.
cloudAgentForm.baseModelHelp: The tool-calling + coding model this agent runs on — pick one of your LLMs or a model from the pool. A run pins one model for the whole task; leave default to use the plan's best coding model.
cloudAgentForm.personalityHelp: Give this agent a personality with a trait test or sliders. It shapes how the agent reasons, how carefully it works, and how it communicates on every run.
cloudAgentForm.capabilitiesHint: Skills and personas assigned here travel with this agent everywhere it runs — Builder, Workflow, on-prem or cloud — independent of any project.

step1.title: Design your dataset
step1.body: Open the Brain (button in the bottom-right) to draft instruction/response pairs and reason about architecture. Datasets are stored per-project and feed training.

step2.title: Train a LoRA adapter
step2.body: Fine-tune a base model in-browser via WebGPU. Each run produces a portable LoRA artifact you can evaluate and iterate on.
step2.metric: {runs, plural, one {# run} other {# runs}} · {trained} trained

step3.title: Benchmark your model
step3.body: Score an EvermindLM on held-out text — perplexity, accuracy, throughput — entirely on-device. Measure quality before you publish, and see what to improve.

step4.title: Publish to the Workforce
step4.body: Bundle your trained adapter (optionally with Mamba memory) into an agent package and publish it to the Workforce Registry.

step5.title: Export your model
step5.body: Download your trained model as a portable artifact — a Hugging Face repo, ONNX, safetensors, or GGUF.

seo.title: Evermind — The Builderforce.ai LLM, a Self-Updating Model
seo.description: Evermind is Builderforce.ai's project model and memory system. Its keyed write-through updates are designed to replace superseded project facts and make current context available to supported browser and agent workflows.

law.heading: Write-Through Cognition
law.lead: Every frozen frontier model shares one flaw: its knowledge is fixed at training time, and every update is a bolt-on. Evermind is governed by a single principle that removes the bolt-on entirely.
law.quote: Evermind is Builderforce.ai's project model and memory system, designed to keep maintained project facts current through keyed updates that replace superseded context.
law.figcap: Conventional models append and reconcile; Evermind upserts by key and invalidates — there is no reconcile step.

architecture.heading: One brain, three cooperating layers
architecture.lead: Evermind isn't a monolith. It's three layers working together — the same three the hero animation lights up as information travels through it.
architecture.figcap: One brain, all yours: Evermind's own generator as the cortex, its write-through hippocampus for memory, and a limbic layer for dynamics. (External frontier models stay routable when you want them — just not required.)

pillars.title: Write-Through Cognition
pillars.desc: Project facts use stable keys so an accepted update can replace prior context instead of simply appending another copy. Provenance and evaluation remain essential when the source itself is incomplete or wrong.

pillars.title: Shared-expert hybrid generator
pillars.desc: A dense always-on backbone carries continuous online learning, while lazily-loaded routed SSM experts page in on demand. You get specialist depth without a giant frozen blob — and it runs on WebGPU with zero runtime dependencies.

pillars.title: Write-through memory
pillars.desc: Maintained facts upsert by stable key and invalidate prior recall for that key, reducing stale duplicate context and making corrections explicit.

pillars.title: Limbic dynamics
pillars.desc: A trainable affective layer modulates how the model responds in the moment — personality as setpoints, limbic state as dynamics — so agents behave consistently with the persona you give them.

contrast.heading: Evermind vs. a frozen frontier model
contrast.lead: Evermind isn't built to out-parameter the biggest models. It wins on the axes their architecture structurally trades away.
contrast.figcap: The whole argument in one frame — a frozen model needs a bolt-on for every update; Evermind inverts all five axes.

lifecycle.lead: Train a supported model in the browser, benchmark it, validate it with an API call, publish it to your Workforce Registry, and invoke it from compatible applications or agents.

steps.desc: Fine-tune supported LoRA adapters with WebGPU and create a persistent memory snapshot locally. Connected evaluation or publishing steps may transmit the data they require.

faq.question: What is Evermind?
faq.answer: Evermind is the Builderforce.ai LLM — the self-updating model at the brain of the platform. It is governed by Write-Through Cognition: new knowledge is written straight through into the model, so an update replaces what came before with no reconciliation step, and reads always reflect the latest truth. Evermind is built from a shared-expert hybrid SSM generator (a dense always-on backbone plus lazily-loaded routed experts), a write-through knowledge memory, and a trainable limbic layer for dynamics, and it runs on WebGPU in the browser, on-device, or inside every agent.

faq.question: What is the Builderforce.ai LLM?
faq.answer: The Builderforce.ai LLM is Evermind. Rather than relying on a frozen third-party frontier model, Builderforce.ai runs its own self-updating model that learns as it works. Frontier LLMs can still be routed to when you want them, but Evermind is the native model that gives the platform currency (never stale), a small footprint (runs on-device), and full ownership (your data, open packages, no third-party model dependency).

faq.question: What is Write-Through Cognition?
faq.answer: Write-Through Cognition is the governing principle of Evermind. Knowledge is written straight through into the model, so an update is an upsert by a stable key plus an invalidation of the old recall — an update means replace, not append. Reads always reflect the latest truth and there is never a stale-then-reconcile step. It is the same invalidate-on-write rule used for caching, applied to a model's knowledge tier so it can never quietly drift out of date.

faq.question: How is Evermind different from a frozen LLM like GPT or Claude?
faq.answer: Frozen frontier models fix their knowledge at training time; updating them means a bolt-on retrain, fine-tune, RAG pipeline, or hand-edit — each a separate reconciliation step. Evermind writes new knowledge directly into the model, so it never accumulates contradictory copies of the same fact and never needs a reconcile pass. It is designed to win not on raw parameter count but on three axes a frozen model structurally trades away: currency, footprint, and ownership.

faq.question: Does Evermind run on-device or in the browser?
faq.answer: Yes. Evermind runs on WebGPU, so it executes in the browser, on-device, or embedded inside every agent, with zero runtime dependencies. The same model and its write-through memory travel wherever the agent runs, which is what lets agents carry correct knowledge across sessions without a cloud round-trip.

faq.question: Can I use Evermind inside my own agents?
faq.answer: Yes. Evermind is the model behind the platform's agents, and its write-through memory and recall are available to the agents you run — so a corrected fact stays corrected across sessions. You can also train custom specialist models in the browser (WebGPU LoRA) and publish them to the Workforce Registry to call from inside your own agent.

faq.question: How does Evermind stay up to date without retraining?
faq.answer: Through its shared-expert hybrid generator and write-through memory. A dense always-on backbone carries continuous online learning while routed experts page in on demand, and every new fact upserts by a stable key and invalidates its prior recall. New knowledge lands in the model the moment it happens, so there is no retrain cycle and no knowledge cutoff you do not control.

faq.question: Does Evermind have benchmarks — how do I know a model I train is any good?
faq.answer: Yes. Every model you train in the Studio is scored on-device before you publish it. The built-in benchmarking harness holds out a slice of your corpus the model never trains on, then reports the standard language-model yardsticks — held-out perplexity, bits-per-token, top-1 and top-k next-token accuracy, and generation throughput — and can A/B two checkpoints so you can see whether a fresh adaptation actually improved on the last one. It runs entirely in your browser with no GPU bill and no data leaving your machine, so you publish on evidence, not vibes. The same harness is the open measurement instrument behind the Evermind technical report.

faq.question: Can Evermind learn from a frontier model like Opus or Mistral?
faq.answer: Yes — through teacher distillation. You can pin any frontier LLM (Opus, Mistral, GLM and more) as a teacher for a project’s Evermind. For each real task your team ships, the teacher is asked for the ideal answer through the metered gateway, and the SSM adapts on the pair of (task context → teacher exemplar) rather than on the raw run text. Over time your own small, on-device model absorbs the quality of a much larger one, while you keep ownership and currency. The teacher call is cost-gated to your token budget and best-effort — a miss falls back to learning from the raw work — so distillation never stalls the learning loop.

features.title: Evermind — The Self-Updating Model
features.shortDesc: A project model designed to learn as the work changes.
features.longDesc: Evermind is the brain of the platform — a self-updating model governed by Write-Through Cognition: new knowledge is written straight through, so an update replaces what came before with no reconciliation step. A shared-expert hybrid generator (dense backbone + routed SSM experts) learns online and runs on WebGPU, so it wins on currency, footprint, and ownership rather than raw scale — in the browser, on-device, or inside every agent.

features.title: Distill a Frontier Model Into Your Own
features.shortDesc: Pin any frontier model as a teacher and train your own private model on its best answers.
features.longDesc: Pin any frontier LLM — Opus, Mistral, GLM and more — as a teacher for a project’s Evermind. For every real piece of work your team ships, the teacher produces the ideal answer to that task and your own model learns from it, steadily absorbing frontier-level quality into a small model you own and run on-device. It’s cost-gated and best-effort: it only spends when there’s token budget, and a teacher miss falls back to learning from the raw work so a lesson is never lost.

features.title: A Learning Brain for Every Project
features.shortDesc: Every project gets its own self-updating model that learns from your team’s work.
features.longDesc: Each project is provisioned with its own Evermind on day one — a self-updating model that learns from every run across all four studios: design, voice, LLM, and video. Corrections stick across sessions through a shared write-through fact store, so the brain that helped yesterday is smarter today. Inference stays off until you opt in, and the model is editable right in the LLM Studio.

features.title: Agentic Workforce Kanban
features.shortDesc: Staff a deep role roster of humans and AI agents on a sign-off-gated board.
features.longDesc: Go beyond a to-do list: staff each project from a first-class job-role taxonomy — humans and AI agents in the same roster — starting from a recommended set built for your team. Swimlanes can require the right reviewer before a ticket advances, and every "Done" carries a per-ticket role and diagnostic sign-off audit, so quality is gated at the board rather than hoped for after the fact.

features.title: Kanban Template Marketplace
features.shortDesc: Buy, sell, and install ready-made board templates with lanes, roles, and gates.
features.longDesc: Package a delivery process — lanes, required roles, review gates, and a recommended roster — as a Kanban template, then publish it to the marketplace to sell or share. Install a proven template into any project in one click, so a team inherits a governed, role-gated workflow instead of assembling one from scratch.

features.title: Validator Agent — Proof of Done
features.shortDesc: An agent that checks "Done" really is done and files the gaps it finds.
features.longDesc: Ad-hoc chat work becomes visible tickets automatically, and a built-in Validator agent reviews every item marked Done — recording a verdict and opening GAP tasks for anything that falls short. One shared merge-to-Done path covers human approval, green CI, and post-deploy, so nothing slips through as "finished" without proof.

features.title: Learned Model Routing
features.shortDesc: The platform learns which model is best — and cheapest — for each kind of task.
features.longDesc: Every run is scored on its outcome, and a learned router reorders which model handles each action type accordingly — cheaper models take the work they do well, premium models are reserved for where they earn it. Combined with the semantic cache, your token bill bends down as the platform learns your workload, with a one-flag kill switch whenever you want manual control.

features.title: Kanban Board & Project Management
features.shortDesc: Plan, assign & track work on a live agent Kanban board.
features.longDesc: A full project-management surface: organize work into projects, then plan, assign, and track every task on a live Kanban board — swimlanes per status or per agent, plus table, calendar, and Gantt views. Humans and AI agents sit on the same board, and work flows from backlog to done in real time.

features.title: Train Your Own Agents — Then Use Them Inside Your Agent
features.shortDesc: Train custom agents and call them from inside your agent.
features.longDesc: Close the loop: train a custom agent (in-browser WebGPU LoRA + AI evaluation), publish it to the Workforce Registry, then hire it and call it from inside your own agent. Your trained specialists become tools your main agent delegates to — a fully agentic workforce you own and orchestrate.

features.title: A VS Code Surface for Engineering Teams
features.shortDesc: Bring canvas context, agents, review, and delivery into the editor.
features.longDesc: The BuilderForce VS Code extension gives engineering teams an editor-native view of relevant platform work: chat with agents, add repository and diagnostic context, assign tasks, review changes, and handle approvals close to the code.

features.title: Agentic Tester — Autonomous QA
features.shortDesc: An AI agent that browser-tests your app on a schedule.
features.longDesc: The Agentic Tester is a hireable QA agent. Point it at your project's URL, save the logins it should use, and it drives a real browser through your highest-traffic flows — ranking what to test from real usage heatmaps, logging in as each persona, and capturing console errors, failed requests, and crashes. Run it on demand or schedule it as part of a workflow; every bug it finds lands straight on your Kanban board.

features.title: Hire Human Talent
features.shortDesc: Bring on freelance developers, DBAs and designers — and pay only for tracked time.
features.longDesc: Beyond AI agents, hire real people: the Talent Marketplace lists vetted freelance developers, DBAs, designers and specialists with résumés (powered by hired.video), skills and hourly rates. Interview, hire across any project, and see billable hours captured automatically from the work they do in the portal and VS Code — every timecard is yours to approve before you pay. Humans and agents work side by side on the same board.

features.title: Model Studio & Agent Training
features.shortDesc: Train, evaluate, and publish specialist models and agents.
features.longDesc: Use in-browser WebGPU LoRA fine-tuning, evaluation, and publishing tools to create specialist models and make them available to supported agent workflows.

features.title: Connected Systems & Orchestration
features.shortDesc: Connect supported tools and coordinate work across them.
features.longDesc: Connect supported systems such as GitHub, Jira, and Confluence with encrypted credentials, then make approved operations available through workflows and the Brain tool registry.

features.title: Agent Governance & Security
features.shortDesc: Apply permissions, approvals, isolation, and execution records.
features.longDesc: Keep accountable people in control with role-based access, human approval gates for configured actions, tenant isolation, encrypted integration credentials, and retained execution records.

features.title: Planning Spine — Portfolio to Task
features.shortDesc: One dated, cost-bearing hierarchy on a single Gantt.
features.longDesc: Plan, deliver, and account for work on one hierarchy: portfolio → initiative → epic → task, with Objectives and Key Results attaching at any level. Every leaf's cost — LLM spend priced at write time plus human effort — rolls up to every ancestor and is split CAPEX vs OPEX, with anomaly flags where a capitalization decision needs sign-off. Engineering plans on it, the PMO rolls portfolios up on it, and finance closes from it — one set of numbers, no reconciliation step.

features.title: Error Observability + One-Click Agent Fix
features.shortDesc: Crash to pull request on a single surface.
features.longDesc: Ingest runtime errors from your browser SDK, OpenTelemetry, Sentry, PostHog, or LogRocket; group them by fingerprint into deduplicated error groups with occurrence and affected-user counts; then turn any group into a fix task a cloud agent picks up and ships as a pull request. Observability that doesn't end at a dashboard — the same platform that surfaces the crash assigns it, fixes it, and PRs it.

features.title: Knowledge Management & Compliance
features.shortDesc: Versioned SOPs with an audit-ready acknowledgement trail.
features.longDesc: A versioned base for SOPs, processes, and docs with immutable publish snapshots, timestamped read-acknowledgements, and per-user overdue tracking — audit-ready evidence for SOX, TISAX, and ISO 27001. Author and improve documents with AI, co-edit in real time, and gate access per page. The same knowledge that proves compliance also grounds your agents.

features.title: Single-Pane Board Connectors
features.shortDesc: Two-way sync with Jira, Linear, Sentry, PagerDuty & more.
features.longDesc: Connect the trackers and incident tools you already run — Jira, Linear, monday, Asana, ClickUp, ServiceNow, Freshservice, Sentry, PagerDuty, and GitHub — and sync work two-ways. Agents pick up and act on a ticket or incident wherever it originates, and changes flow back to the system of record. One pane to orchestrate across everything, with no migration and no lock-in.

features.title: AI Dataset Generation
features.shortDesc: Generate datasets from a single prompt.
features.longDesc: Generate instruction-tuning datasets from a single capability prompt using any OpenRouter model. Export as JSONL, stored in R2.

features.title: In-Browser LoRA Training
features.shortDesc: Fine-tune up to 2B params with WebGPU.
features.longDesc: Fine-tune models up to 2B parameters directly in Chrome with WebGPU. No cloud GPU bills, zero round-trips, total privacy.

features.title: Grounded RAG & Answer Evaluation
features.shortDesc: Hybrid retrieval, plus faithfulness & drift scoring.
features.longDesc: The full retrieval-and-evaluation stack, built in. Memory uses hybrid retrieval — dense embeddings and BM25 keyword search fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion and reranked with MMR for relevance and diversity, over chunked documents. Every run is then scored for faithfulness, answer relevance, and hallucination rate, and a drift monitor flags when a model's quality regresses over time — so a wrong answer never hides behind a green dashboard.

features.title: AI Evaluation Engine
features.shortDesc: Score outputs with an AI judge.
features.longDesc: Score your model outputs with an independent AI judge. Get structured quality metrics: correctness, reasoning, hallucination rate.

features.title: Agent Registry
features.shortDesc: Publish agents to the Workforce Registry.
features.longDesc: Publish your trained agent to the public Workforce Registry with a profile, skills, and eval score. Others can hire it instantly.

features.title: R2 Artifact Storage
features.shortDesc: Persist LoRA weights to Cloudflare R2.
features.longDesc: LoRA adapter weights are serialised from WebGPU buffers and automatically persisted to Cloudflare R2 with signed URLs.

features.title: Semantic Response Cache
features.shortDesc: Reuse answers across paraphrases — slash token spend.
features.longDesc: An embedding-keyed cache reuses a prior answer when a new prompt means the same thing as one already answered, so the frontier model is never billed twice for the same work. Two tiers: a free on-device layer (SSM embeddings, in your browser and in each agent) plus a shared gateway layer — so a cache hit in the web app saves tokens for your agents too.

features.title: Canvas Builder Workspace
features.shortDesc: Monaco editor, terminal, preview, and AI chat in one engineering workspace.
features.longDesc: Monaco editor, terminal, AI chat, file explorer — everything you need in one collaborative project workspace.

features.title: Secure Multi-Tenant
features.shortDesc: JWT auth with tenant isolation.
features.longDesc: JWT auth with tenant isolation. Projects, datasets, models, and agents are private and scoped per tenant by default.

features.title: Cloudflare Edge
features.shortDesc: A globally distributed Worker API for responsive platform services.
features.longDesc: Cloudflare Workers provide globally distributed API execution. COOP/COEP headers enable SharedArrayBuffer where browser-based model tooling requires it.

faq.question: Is Builderforce.ai an alternative to GitHub Copilot?
faq.answer: Yes, but they solve different scopes. GitHub Copilot is single-agent autocomplete inside VS Code, tied to GPT and Claude models. Builderforce.ai is a self-hosted, MIT-licensed multi-agent platform that orchestrates seven specialist roles through full planning, bug-fix, refactor and adversarial-review workflows, runs on 30+ model providers including local Ollama, and adds approvals, audit and persistent memory. Teams that have outgrown line completion adopt Builderforce.ai for end-to-end delivery.

faq.question: How does Builderforce.ai compare to Cursor and Windsurf?
faq.answer: Cursor and Windsurf are excellent AI-native editors, but they are still single-agent and IDE-bound. Builderforce.ai is IDE-independent and works from any channel or CLI, coordinates multiple agents on one task through a dependency DAG, and is fully self-hosted with model freedom across 30+ providers. You can even connect Cursor or Windsurf to Builderforce.ai over MCP and use it as your orchestration and memory layer.

faq.question: Builderforce.ai vs Claude Code and Aider, what is the difference?
faq.answer: Claude Code is locked to Anthropic models and Aider runs a single CLI agent. Builderforce.ai runs a team of specialist agents with a built-in adversarial review pass, human approval gates, an audit trail, and persistent project memory in .builderforce/. It is model-agnostic across 30+ providers and adds fleet mesh, remote:<id> dispatch and 15+ chat channels, so it scales from one developer to an orchestrated fleet.

faq.question: Builderforce.ai vs Devin and OpenHands, which should I pick for autonomous engineering?
faq.answer: Devin is a proprietary hosted autonomous agent and OpenHands is an open single-agent runtime. Builderforce.ai differs by being self-hosted and MIT-licensed with true multi-agent orchestration and governance built in: approval gates, audit trails and self-healing recovery that auto-detects failures and reruns affected steps. You keep your code on your own infrastructure and choose any model, including local ones.

faq.question: Can Builderforce.ai run fully offline or air-gapped?
faq.answer: Yes. Builderforce.ai is self-hosted and supports air-gapped deployment. With local models via Ollama you can run the entire agent workforce without any code or prompt leaving your network, which most closed competitors cannot offer. Project memory persists locally in .builderforce/ so context survives across sessions without a cloud dependency.

faq.question: Does Builderforce.ai lock me into one model or IDE?
faq.answer: No. Builderforce.ai is model-agnostic across 30+ providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock and local Ollama, and it is IDE-independent, reachable from any CLI or chat channel. There is no editor fork to adopt and no single-vendor model requirement, which is a core difference from Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf and Claude Code.

homepageFaq.question: Do I need an account to start?
homepageFaq.answer: No. The first canvas is private and local to your browser—nothing leaves the device until you sign in. When you do, the draft you already started is claimed into your workspace rather than discarded.

homepageFaq.question: What exactly are the AI agents?
homepageFaq.answer: Specialists that hold a role on your team—a CFO, a CMO, a CTO, and others. They sit along the bottom of every canvas beside the people you invited. Bring one onto the board and it reads the work, takes the assignment, and produces a change you can review.

homepageFaq.question: Where do the numbers in my deck come from?
homepageFaq.answer: Your ledger. Connect Stripe, Xero or QuickBooks and the runway, burn, ARR and cohort figures are computed from the transactions and carry the date they were read — so a figure with no source behind it is flagged before an investor finds it, rather than being retyped into a slide and quietly going stale.

homepageFaq.question: Who can see my data room?
homepageFaq.answer: Only the people you invite, on the terms you set: an NDA to sign, a watermark carrying their name, an expiry date, and a record of every file they opened. Access is granted to the investor rather than to a folder, so one revocation reaches every room and update — and it can be revoked at any time.

homepageFaq.question: Can I use my own model?
homepageFaq.answer: Yes. Connect your own provider account and your work runs on it. When a workspace has no connection, the platform’s routing picks a model and the cost lands against your workspace meter.

homepageFaq.question: How is this different from an AI chat tool?
homepageFaq.answer: A chat tool produces text you then have to move somewhere. Builderforce produces connected objects—a live page, a running workflow, or a bound dataset—that reference each other and carry a reviewable history from the first idea to production.

homepageFaq.question: What happens to work an agent does on its own?
homepageFaq.answer: Every change has an author and a diff. Anything that touches production, sends on your behalf, or exceeds a spending limit waits for a named human approver on the board.

faq.question: What is Evermind?
faq.answer: Evermind is the brain of Builderforce.ai — a self-updating model governed by Write-Through Cognition. Instead of freezing knowledge at training time like a conventional frontier model, Evermind writes new knowledge straight through into the model, so an update replaces what came before with no reconciliation step and reads always reflect the latest truth. It is built from a shared-expert hybrid generator (a dense backbone that learns online plus routed SSM experts that page in on demand), a write-through knowledge memory that upserts by stable key, and a trainable limbic layer for dynamics. It runs on WebGPU in the browser, on-device, or inside every agent, and is designed to win on currency, footprint, and ownership rather than raw scale.

faq.question: What is Builderforce.ai?
faq.answer: Builderforce.ai is a creative canvas where teams and AI agents turn ideas into working outcomes. You can create websites, workflows, prototypes, data stories, models, documents, and delivery plans in one visual workspace, preserve the relationships between them, and move approved work into governed execution.

faq.question: Is Builderforce.ai an enterprise platform?
faq.answer: Yes. Teams can begin with a private canvas, then add shared workspaces, role-based access, approval workflows, delivery tracking, cost visibility, and audit evidence as the work grows. Creative and operational teams keep one connected record instead of reconstructing decisions across separate whiteboards, documents, project tools, and agent chats.

faq.question: Can I train my own agents and use them inside my own agent?
faq.answer: Yes — that is the core loop. Train a custom agent in the browser with WebGPU LoRA fine-tuning and the AI evaluation engine, publish it to the Workforce Registry, then hire it and call it from inside your own agent. Your trained specialists become tools your main agent delegates to, so you build and orchestrate a fully agentic workforce you own.

faq.question: Do I have to leave VS Code to manage my agents?
faq.answer: No. Builderforce.ai is a web-first creative canvas. Engineering teams can also use the BuilderForce VS Code extension to bring repository context, diagnostics, agent work, reviews, and approvals closer to the code.

faq.question: Does Builderforce have a Kanban board and project management?
faq.answer: Yes. Projects organize your work, and the task board tracks it on a live Kanban board with swimlanes per status or per agent, plus table, calendar, and Gantt views. Humans and AI agents share the same board, so you plan, assign, and watch work flow from backlog to done in real time.

faq.question: Can the Kanban board run itself with AI agents?
faq.answer: Yes — that is Autonomous Swimlane Execution. Assign an agent (Cloud or On-Premise) to a board lane and tickets in that lane are dispatched to it automatically; the board advances from lane to lane as agents finish, pausing only at the approval gates you choose. You manage outcomes on a board instead of issuing prompts one at a time.

faq.question: How does Builderforce keep LLM token costs down?
faq.answer: A cross-surface semantic cache reuses a prior answer when a new prompt means the same thing as one already answered, so the frontier model is never billed twice for the same work. It runs in two tiers — a free on-device layer using SSM embeddings (in the browser and in each agent) and a shared tenant-scoped gateway layer — and is combined with model routing that exhausts cheaper models before reaching premium ones.

faq.question: Can I plan and cost work from portfolio down to task?
faq.answer: Yes — that is the Planning Spine. Portfolio, initiative, epic, and task live on one dated hierarchy (with Objectives and Key Results attaching at any level), rendered as a single Gantt. Because every task is instrumented, its cost — LLM spend priced at write time plus human effort — rolls up to every ancestor and is split CAPEX vs OPEX, with anomaly flags where a capitalization decision needs sign-off. Engineering, the PMO, and finance read the same numbers, and the whole spine exports to CSV.

faq.question: Can Builderforce fix the errors it monitors?
faq.answer: Yes. The Quality pillar ingests runtime errors from a browser SDK, OpenTelemetry, Sentry, PostHog, or LogRocket, groups them by fingerprint into deduplicated error groups, then turns any group into a fix task a cloud agent picks up and ships as a pull request. Unlike a monitoring dashboard that ends at a stack trace, the same platform that surfaces the crash assigns it, fixes it, and opens the PR.

faq.question: Do I have to migrate off Jira or Linear to use Builderforce?
faq.answer: No. Board connectors sync work two-ways with the tools you already run — Jira, Linear, monday, Asana, ClickUp, ServiceNow, Freshservice, Sentry, PagerDuty, and GitHub. Agents pick up and act on a ticket or incident wherever it originates, and changes flow back to the system of record. You get one pane to orchestrate across everything with no migration and no lock-in.

faq.question: Is Builderforce free?
faq.answer: Yes — the Free tier is $0/month forever with no credit card required. It includes WebGPU training, dataset generation, AI evaluation, and public Workforce browsing. The Pro plan unlocks private agents, unlimited training, and priority support.

faq.question: How do I train a model in my browser?
faq.answer: Start a project, generate or upload a dataset, then launch the in-browser LoRA training wizard. Training runs entirely on your local WebGPU device — no cloud GPUs are required, and your data never leaves your browser.

faq.question: What is the Workforce Registry?
faq.answer: The Workforce Registry is a public marketplace where trained AI agents can be listed with profiles, skills, and evaluation scores. Other teams and applications can discover and hire agents instantly.

faq.question: What is WebGPU LoRA fine-tuning?
faq.answer: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique that trains a small set of adapter weights instead of the full model. Builderforce runs LoRA training directly in your browser using the WebGPU API, supporting models up to 2 billion parameters with zero cloud GPU costs.

faq.question: How does the AI evaluation engine work?
faq.answer: After training, an independent AI judge scores your model's outputs on structured quality metrics including correctness, reasoning quality, and hallucination rate. This gives you objective eval scores before publishing to the Workforce Registry.

faq.question: What models can I fine-tune?
faq.answer: Builderforce supports LoRA fine-tuning of transformer and SSM (State Space Model) architectures up to 2 billion parameters. Training runs on your local GPU via the WebGPU API in Chrome, Edge, or any WebGPU-capable browser.

faq.question: Is my data private during training?
faq.answer: Training computation runs locally on supported WebGPU devices. Data is transmitted only when you use an explicitly connected service such as dataset generation, collaboration, evaluation with a remote model, or artifact publishing; review those steps before enabling them.

faq.question: How does Builderforce compare to cloud training platforms?
faq.answer: Unlike cloud training platforms that charge per GPU-hour, Builderforce runs training on your local WebGPU device at zero cost. It also includes built-in dataset generation, AI evaluation, and a marketplace for publishing agents — features typically requiring multiple separate tools.

faq.question: Can I integrate Builderforce agents with BuilderForce Agents?
faq.answer: Yes — models trained on Builderforce can be exported and published as Evermind models that your self-hosted BuilderForce Agents gateway calls directly as the model, not just as a memory layer. The platform supports the full pipeline: train a custom SSM in the browser, publish it, and route live traffic to it over the OpenAI-compatible API.

faq.question: Can I train my own model on a frontier model’s answers?
faq.answer: Yes — that is teacher distillation. Pin any frontier LLM (Opus, Mistral, GLM and more) as a teacher for a project’s Evermind. For each real piece of work your team ships, the teacher produces the ideal answer to that task, and your own model learns from that exemplar instead of the raw text — so it steadily absorbs frontier-level quality into a small model you own and run on-device. It is cost-gated (it only spends when you have token budget) and best-effort (a teacher miss falls back to learning from the raw work), so a lesson is never lost.

faq.question: Does each project get its own model?
faq.answer: Yes. Every project is provisioned with its own Evermind on creation — a self-updating model that learns from every run across all four studios (design, voice, LLM, and video) through one shared learning mechanism. Corrected facts persist across sessions in a write-through fact store shared by the web app, VS Code, cloud, and on-prem agents, so the brain that helped yesterday is smarter today. Inference stays off until you opt in, and the model is editable in the LLM Studio.

faq.question: Can I gate my board so only the right role can finish a ticket?
faq.answer: Yes — that is the Agentic Workforce Kanban. Staff each project from a first-class job-role taxonomy of humans and AI agents, and configure swimlanes to require the right reviewer before a ticket can advance. Every item marked Done carries a per-ticket role and diagnostic sign-off audit, and a role-coverage diagnostic flags gaps on the board, so quality is enforced rather than assumed.

faq.question: How does Builderforce check that work marked Done is really done?
faq.answer: A built-in Validator agent reviews every item marked Done, records a verdict, and opens GAP tasks for anything that falls short. Ad-hoc chat work is also captured as visible tickets automatically, and one shared merge-to-Done path covers human approval, green CI, and post-deploy — so nothing is reported as finished without proof.

faq.question: Can I buy or sell a Kanban board template?
faq.answer: Yes. Package a delivery process — lanes, required roles, review gates, and a recommended roster — as a Kanban template and publish it to the marketplace to sell or share. Any team can install a proven template into a project in one click and inherit a governed, role-gated workflow instead of building one from scratch.

faq.question: What is BuilderForce Agents?
faq.answer: BuilderForce Agents is the self-hosted agent runtime behind Builderforce.ai. It runs and coordinates independent coding agents and sub-agents on your own infrastructure under the MIT license, with deep codebase understanding, a skills system, multi-agent workflows, and human-in-the-loop approval gates — orchestrated from the Builderforce.ai portal.

faq.question: Is BuilderForce Agents open source and self-hosted?
faq.answer: Yes. It is MIT-licensed and runs on your own infrastructure — no vendor lock-in or subscription ceiling. You can run it fully air-gapped, and with local models via Ollama no code or prompt has to leave your network.

faq.question: How do agents coordinate across machines?
faq.answer: Agents form an AgentHost-to-AgentHost mesh. Work is distributed across a fleet of hosts and routed to the best-matched peer with remote:auto[caps] dispatch; every dispatch is HMAC-signed and Bearer-authenticated, and the portal shows a live telemetry timeline of every action.

faq.question: Can agents ship code on their own?
faq.answer: Yes. A Cloud agent clones the bound repo through a secure server-side git proxy (your Git token never leaves the server), writes the change, pushes a branch, and opens a pull request — headless, no browser open. On-Premise agents do the same on your own machine, and approval gates can require human sign-off before any high-impact step.

workflowBuilder.metaDescription: Drag-and-drop, IPAAS-style canvas for composing your own LLM logic — memory, knowledge-base and training nodes — wired to your agents and run on your own hosts. Visual workflows that actually execute.
workflowBuilder.heading: Agentic Workflow Builder
workflowBuilder.tagline: Compose your LLM logic. Wire your agents. Watch it run.
workflowBuilder.description: A drag-and-drop, IPAAS-style canvas where <term>memory</term>, <term>knowledge base</term> and <term>training</term> are nodes you snap together with your agents — then run on your own hosts. Not a diagram tool: every workflow actually executes.
workflowBuilder.paletteIntro: Most workflow builders stop at HTTP calls and if/else. This one adds the primitives that make agents useful — the LLM-logic nodes are the headline.
workflowBuilder.catalogIntro: MCP servers, LLM platforms, databases, CRMs and data-collection sources — drag any of them onto the canvas.
workflowBuilder.finalCtaBody: Open a blank canvas, drop a trigger, an agent and a memory node, wire them up, and run it on a host — in under a minute.

steps.title: Drag in your nodes
steps.body: Pull triggers, LLM-logic, agents and ETL steps onto the canvas. Every node is configurable in a side panel — no code.

steps.title: Wire the flow
steps.body: Connect nodes to declare dependencies. The graph compiles to a dependency-ordered execution plan automatically.

steps.title: Run on your hosts
steps.body: Hit Run and the workflow is claimed by one of your agent hosts, executed, and streamed back to the live monitoring graph.

capabilities.title: Your LLM logic, as nodes
capabilities.description: Memory recall/write, knowledge-base query/ingest, and model training are first-class nodes — compose them like any other step.

capabilities.title: Your agents as executors
capabilities.description: Drop an Agent Run node, pick a role, runtime and model, and your configured agents do the work — local, cloud, browser or remote mesh.

capabilities.title: Runs you can watch
capabilities.description: Every run instantiates a tracked execution record — task statuses, the live dependency graph, durations and cost land in the monitoring view for free.

capabilities.title: Import, export, version
capabilities.description: Every workflow round-trips to human-authorable YAML — hand-edit it, check it into git, or import a hand-written flow straight onto the canvas.

audit_spreadsheet.label: Audit a spreadsheet
audit_spreadsheet.hint: Check the formulas, find what's wrong and what's fragile.
audit_spreadsheet.brief: Audit a spreadsheet I give you — check the formulas, find the errors and the fragile parts, flag what would break if a row moved or a value changed, and fix what I approve. Show me the issue list before changing anything.

review_draft.label: Review a draft
review_draft.hint: Read it before it goes out and tell me what's weak.
review_draft.brief: Review a draft before I send it — tell me what's unclear, what a sceptical reader would push back on, and what's missing. Mark anything that overstates what we can actually deliver. Give me the specific edits, not general advice.

chase_blockers.label: Chase down blockers
chase_blockers.hint: Find what's stuck, why, and who has to move.
chase_blockers.brief: Find everything that's currently blocked on this project, work out why each one is stuck and who has to move for it to unblock, then open a ticket for each real blocker with the accountable person on it. Tell me which ones I personally need to unstick.

triage_backlog.label: Triage the backlog
triage_backlog.hint: Sort what matters, close what doesn't.
triage_backlog.brief: Go through the backlog and triage it: group duplicates, close what's no longer real, and rank what's left by what it actually unblocks. Tell me the top five and why. Don't delete anything without listing it for me first.

research_and_brief.label: Research and brief me
research_and_brief.hint: Go find out, then write it up with sources.
research_and_brief.brief: Research a question I'll give you: go and read real sources rather than answering from memory, write up what you found with the evidence behind each claim, and be explicit about what you couldn't establish. Then open a follow-up ticket for anything that needs a decision from me.

ship_fix.label: Fix and ship it
ship_fix.hint: Take a defect all the way to a dispatched run.
ship_fix.brief: Take a defect I'll describe, find the root cause rather than the symptom, open it as a tracked ticket with the right owner, and put an agent on it. Tell me the dispatch outcome — if nothing actually started, say exactly what blocked it.

projectEvermind.title: Project Evermind
projectEvermind.description: Give this project its own self-learning model. Once enabled, the project's agents run on it and get sharper with every task they finish — shared across cloud, on-premise, and the editor.
projectEvermind.quarantinedHint: This Evermind auto-disabled after producing incoherent output ({reason}). Retrain it past the coherence bar to re-enable inference.
projectEvermind.targetsHint: Every Evermind this project contributes learning to.
projectEvermind.targetsEmpty: No Everminds resolved for this project yet.
projectEvermind.noModels: Publish a trained model in the LLM Studio first, then enable it here.
projectEvermind.pickModelLabel: Choose a published model to power this project
projectEvermind.inferenceHint: This project's agent runs execute on its Evermind instead of the default model.
projectEvermind.learningHint: Each run teaches the model, shared instantly across every surface.
projectEvermind.teacherHint: Distil a top model (Opus, Mistral, GLM…) into this project's Evermind — pick one and every agent run learns from the frontier model's ideal answer instead of the raw run. You can also teach it a task directly below.
projectEvermind.teacherPaidOnly: Available on paid plans, or connect your own frontier account in Settings ▸ API Keys — teaching uses frontier-model tokens.
projectEvermind.teacherActiveHint: Teaching from {model}. Every agent run — and each task you teach below — is answered by {model}, and your Evermind learns from its ideal answer. There's nothing else to switch on.
projectEvermind.errorGeneric: Something went wrong. Please try again.
projectEvermind.managerOnlyHint: Only a project manager can change these settings.
projectEvermind.notSetUp: This project's Evermind isn't set up yet. A project manager can enable it.
projectEvermind.teachHint: Paste a chat transcript or exemplar to contribute it to the model now.
projectEvermind.teachTextPlaceholder: Paste the transcript or exemplar text…
projectEvermind.taughtDistilled: Taught: {model} answered it and the model learned that answer (v{version}).
projectEvermind.taughtSelf: Taught: learned from your text, with no teacher model (v{version}).
projectEvermind.taughtTeacherFault: Learned, but the teacher {model} produced nothing ({reason}) — so the model learned your raw text, not an ideal answer.
projectEvermind.taughtDropped: Not learned: the merge could not use this contribution.
projectEvermind.taughtStillPending: Still queued — this will merge on the next learning pass.
projectEvermind.teachTeacherHint: Describe a task and {model} answers it — your Evermind learns from the ideal answer. No transcript needed.
projectEvermind.teachTaskPlaceholder: Describe a task to teach — the teacher will answer it…
projectEvermind.inspectEmpty: Nothing learned yet. Runs and teaching will appear here.
projectEvermind.deltaEntry: Weight delta contributed by an agent run.
projectEvermind.validateHint: Check which learned memories would answer this task — before you teach it.
projectEvermind.validateEmpty: No learned memory matches this task yet — teaching it would add new knowledge.
projectEvermind.evalTooltip: Regression check on v{version}: held-out loss {base} → {next} across {size, plural, one {# prior task} other {# prior tasks}}.
projectEvermind.inheritedHint: This build shares its parent project’s Evermind, so everything it has learned is available here. Training and settings live on the parent project.
projectEvermind.testHint: Run a prompt through the model and see exactly what it writes, graded the same way a real reply is. This is how you check the model is worth switching on — before anyone chats with it.
projectEvermind.testPlaceholder: Ask the model something, e.g. “Summarise where this project stands.”
projectEvermind.testRefusedBecause: This would not be shown to a user: {detail}.
projectEvermind.testVerdictReady: This model is coherent enough to serve replies.
projectEvermind.testVerdictNotReady: This model is not coherent enough to serve replies yet. Teach it more, set a teacher model, or re-seed it below.
projectEvermind.maintenanceHint: Repair and tidy the model when it has gone wrong. None of this deletes your project’s work.
projectEvermind.reseedHint: Start over from a known-good base, keeping the project. Use this when the model has trained itself into nonsense. Replies stay switched off until it passes a readiness check again.
projectEvermind.reseedConfirm: Replace this model’s brain with a fresh base? What it has learned so far will no longer shape its answers. This cannot be undone.
projectEvermind.reseedDone: Model replaced — now at v{version}. Run a readiness check before switching replies back on.
projectEvermind.reindexHint: Re-file every memory against the current model. Memories are filed when they are learned, so recall drifts as the model changes — rebuild if it starts recalling the wrong things.
projectEvermind.cleanupHint: Throw away anything queued but not yet learned, and clear cached answers so repeat questions are answered fresh. Learned knowledge is untouched.
projectEvermind.cleanupConfirm: Discard everything queued but not yet learned, and clear cached answers?
projectEvermind.cleanupDone: Discarded {discarded} queued item(s) and cleared {cached} cached answer(s).
projectEvermind.analyzeHint: Read back everything the model has learned and have a frontier model check it for mistakes, stale facts and nonsense — then fix what is wrong by teaching the corrections.
projectEvermind.analyzeVerdict: {verdict, select, incoherent {Nonsense} incorrect {Wrong} outdated {Out of date} unusable {Not an answer} redundant {Duplicate} other {Fine}}
projectEvermind.analyzeApplied: {corrected} corrected and re-taught, {forgotten} removed from recall (already-learned influence is superseded by the correction, not erased). Model is now at v{version}.

policy.title: How this backlog is managed
policy.subtitle: Decide who runs the backlog and how much they do automatically. You can change this any time.

manager.label: Who manages this backlog
manager.help: Pick a teammate or agent to own the backlog, or let the built-in service keep it tidy for you.

enabled.label: Keep this backlog managed
enabled.help: When on, the manager keeps scoring, ranking, and organising work automatically. Turn off to pause everything.

autoBusinessValue.label: Score business value automatically
autoBusinessValue.help: Give every new ticket a value so you can always see what’s worth doing first — no manual guessing.

autoPrioritize.label: Order the backlog for me
autoPrioritize.help: Continuously re-rank the work so the highest-impact tickets rise to the top.

autoAssign.label: Assign owners automatically
autoAssign.help: Hand each ticket to the best-suited teammate or agent so nothing sits unowned.

prMerge.label: When work is finished
prMerge.help: Choose what happens to a pull request once an agent completes a ticket.

immediate.label: Ship right away
immediate.help: Merge and close the pull request as soon as the agent finishes — fastest, best when you trust the checks.

on_green.label: Ship once tests pass
on_green.help: Wait for the automated checks to go green before merging — a safe default.

queue.label: Leave for a human
queue.help: Never merge automatically — hold every pull request for someone to review and merge.

prMerge.needsAuthority: Timing only matters once the manager is allowed to merge — right now merges wait for a person.

allowAutoMerge.label: Let the manager merge pull requests
allowAutoMerge.help: This is permission to merge at all — separate from the timing choice below. When off, the manager still prepares and checks everything, then leaves the merge to a person.

requireSignoff.label: Require sign-off before finishing
requireSignoff.help: Off unless you turn it on. When on, a ticket only finishes — and its pull request only merges — once every required reviewer has signed off, and the manager keeps chasing the roles that still owe one. A ticket nobody was asked to review never qualifies.

effective.title: In effect right now
effective.help: What the manager will actually do once every level of these settings is combined. For permissions, the strictest answer wins.

policy.workspaceDefaultsHint: Anything left on “Use default” follows your workspace defaults in Settings → AI Manager.

ceremonies.sectionHelp: What the manager may do when it runs a standup or planning session and the people it concerns are not there.

allowUnattendedCeremonies.label: Run ceremonies without people
allowUnattendedCeremonies.help: Lets the manager conduct a scheduled standup nobody joined. Off: the session is still recorded, showing that nobody attended, but nothing is decided on the team’s behalf.

allowAgentReassignment.label: Hand stale work to agents
allowAgentReassignment.help: Lets a ceremony move a ticket from someone who missed it onto an agent. Missing a ceremony is never enough on its own — the ticket must also have sat untouched for the period below.

allowAutoStaffLanes.label: Configure a stage that names nobody
allowAutoStaffLanes.help: Some stages authorise no role at all — no required role declared, no agent staffed — so on a lifecycle-managed board nothing sitting in them can ever be dispatched. The manager always reports these; this decides whether it may also fix one by pinning a producer to the stage. Granting it starts every ticket already waiting there, so a stage left empty on purpose (an intake column you pull from by hand) should stay that way.

agentReassignIdleHours.label: Only after the ticket is idle for
agentReassignIdleHours.help: How long a ticket must sit untouched before an absent owner’s claim on it lapses. Long enough that a normal absence never reaches it.

agentReassignMaxPerSession.label: At most, per ceremony
agentReassignMaxPerSession.help: Hard limit on how many tickets one ceremony may hand over, so a single standup can never quietly re-home a whole sprint.

autoSchedule.label: Put the work on a timeline
autoSchedule.help: Give undated tickets a start and due date in ranked order, respecting what blocks what. Never changes a date you set yourself.

seo.title: SOC 2 Readiness Audit — Automated, During Onboarding | Builderforce
seo.description: Run an automated SOC 2 readiness audit across your GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps repos during signup. Get a scored report mapped to the Common Criteria (CC1–CC9) and an agent-opened remediation PR.

soc2.sub: Create a project, connect your ticket system and repos, and Builderforce files a ticket for the security agent to audit your code against the SOC 2 Common Criteria — then opens a remediation PR. You get a scored report, not a checklist.

visualSection.title: What your report looks like
visualSection.sub: An overall readiness score, every Common-Criteria family graded pass / partial / gap, the concrete findings, and a remediation pull request already opened.

criteria.title: Mapped to the Common Criteria
criteria.sub: Every finding rolls up to a SOC 2 Common-Criteria family, so your report reads the way an auditor thinks.

items.label: Control environment — ownership and CODEOWNERS across every repo.
Communication & policies — SECURITY.md and contributor guidelines.
Risk assessment & control activities — CI gates on the default branch.
Logical access & secrets hygiene — no committed keys or credentials.
System operations — pinned dependencies and reproducible builds.
Change management — tests plus mandatory review before merge.
Vendor & risk mitigation — a documented security disclosure process.

how.title: How the audit runs
how.sub: The onboarding wizard turns signup into a delivered report.

steps.title: Create a project
steps.desc: Name your project in the setup wizard — it becomes the home for your audit reports.

steps.title: Connect repos & tickets
steps.desc: Attach GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps repos and your Jira / Monday board.

steps.title: Run the audit
steps.desc: A ticket is filed for the security agent, which scans your repos and opens a remediation PR.

steps.title: Read your report

family.title: One flow, five system audits
family.sub: The same one-click audit runs across every dimension of your engineering org.

items.name: SOC 2 Readiness
items.desc: Repos and controls mapped to the Common Criteria (CC1–CC9).

items.name: Architecture
items.desc: Design-principle adherence: DRY, SOLID, DDD, and patterns.

items.name: Quality
items.desc: Testing, CI, and build-integrity signals across your repos.

items.name: Product Vision & Roadmap
items.desc: Objectives, key results, roadmap, and a documented vision.

items.name: Privacy & Data-Law
items.desc: GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and CAN-SPAM readiness from your code.

faq.question: Is this a SOC 2 certification?
faq.answer: No — it's a readiness audit. It produces an automated, evidence-backed report mapped to the SOC 2 Common Criteria so you know exactly what to close before a formal Type I or Type II examination.

faq.question: How does the audit run during signup?
faq.answer: The onboarding wizard creates a project, connects your ticket system and repositories, then files a ticket for the security agent. The audit scores an instant report and dispatches the agent to open a remediation pull request — you're notified when it's ready.

faq.question: Which repositories can it scan?
faq.answer: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps — one or many per project. Tokens stay server-side; the audit reads the repository tree to derive its signals.

faq.question: What other audits are included?
faq.answer: The same flow runs an Architecture analysis, a Quality audit, a Product Vision & Roadmap audit, and a Privacy & Data-Law (GDPR / CCPA / CAN-SPAM) audit — each a scored project report.

finalCta.title: Get your SOC 2 report today
finalCta.sub: Sign up, connect a repo, and your first readiness report lands in minutes.

train.label: Train
train.blurb: Train an Evermind model on a dataset (tokenizer → train → package).

trainTokenizer.label: Train Tokenizer
trainTokenizer.blurb: Learn a byte-BPE tokenizer from a corpus.

datasetQuality.label: Dataset Quality
datasetQuality.blurb: Gate the corpus: min words/sequences + max duplicate ratio.

trainModel.label: Train Model
trainModel.blurb: Train an EvermindLM on the corpus (on-device, CPU).

roundtrip.label: Package (Round-trip)
roundtrip.blurb: Package → reload → prove identical output. Emits the .evermind artifact.

export.label: Export
export.blurb: Export a publishable repo (Hugging Face / ONNX / safetensors / GGUF).

distillCorpus.label: Distil Corpus
distillCorpus.blurb: Build a (prompt → completion) corpus from teacher exemplars (JSON pairs).

codeBenchmark.label: Code Benchmark (pass@1)
codeBenchmark.blurb: Held-out pass@1 on unseen prompts (JSON tasks).

filter.label: Filter
filter.blurb: Drop the payload unless a predicate holds. Pair with Router/Branch: filter on $route == "Name" to gate one path.

branch.label: Branch
branch.blurb: Tags the payload with $branch (true/false) from a condition — pair with a Filter reading $branch to gate one side.

output.label: Output
output.blurb: Terminal: write artifact / notify / push to board.

router.label: Router / If-Else
router.blurb: N-way conditional fan-out — tags the payload with $route (the first matching route's name, or the fallback). Pair with a Filter reading $route == "Name" on each downstream path.

merge.label: Merge
merge.blurb: Join multiple upstream branches back into one payload.

setVariable.label: Set Variable
setVariable.blurb: Write a variable for the rest of THIS run to read (not shared across runs).

getVariable.label: Get Variable
getVariable.blurb: Read a variable set earlier in THIS run.

increment.label: Increment
increment.blurb: A counter that PERSISTS ACROSS RUNS of this workflow (unlike Set/Get Variable) — returns the new value.

sleep.label: Sleep
sleep.blurb: Delay this path by N seconds before continuing.

regexMatch.label: Match Pattern
regexMatch.blurb: Match a regular expression against the input; outputs matches + capture groups.

htmlToText.label: HTML to Text
htmlToText.blurb: Strip HTML tags from the input, leaving plain text.

assert.label: Assert
assert.blurb: Fail (or just warn) the run unless an expression holds — makes a bad upstream state visible in run history instead of silently continuing.

healthcheck.label: Healthcheck
healthcheck.blurb: Probe a URL and report whether it returned the expected status.

webSearch.label: Web Search
webSearch.blurb: Search the open web and return results with page content — resolves your connected Tavily/Ollama/Exa/Linkup key, then an operator SearXNG instance, then a keyless encyclopedic fallback, so it always returns something.

switch.label: Switch
switch.blurb: Fan-out by matching a value against literal cases — tags the payload with $route. Pair with a Filter reading $route == "Name" on each downstream path.

numericAggregator.label: Numeric Aggregator
numericAggregator.blurb: Reduce multiple upstream branches to one number — sum, average, min, max, or count.

tableAggregator.label: Table Aggregator
tableAggregator.blurb: Collect multiple upstream branches' JSON-object outputs into one array of rows.

textAggregator.label: Text Aggregator
textAggregator.blurb: Join multiple upstream branches' text outputs into one string.

setVariables.label: Set Multiple Variables
setVariables.blurb: Write several run-scoped variables at once.

getVariables.label: Get Multiple Variables
getVariables.blurb: Read several variables set earlier in THIS run — outputs one JSON object.

composeString.label: Compose a String
composeString.blurb: Build a string from a '{{input}}' template.

convertEncoding.label: Convert Encoding
convertEncoding.blurb: Base64 / URL / hex encode or decode the input.

htmlTable.label: Get Content from HTML Table
htmlTable.blurb: Search the input HTML for a table and return its rows and columns as text.

htmlElements.label: Get Elements from HTML
htmlElements.blurb: Extract every matching tag from the input HTML, with its text and attributes.

matchElements.label: Match Elements
matchElements.blurb: Get Elements from HTML, filtered to those whose text matches a pattern.

matchPatternAdvanced.label: Match Pattern (Advanced)
matchPatternAdvanced.blurb: Every match of a regular expression, each with its named capture groups as a structured object.

replace.label: Replace
replace.blurb: Find and replace — literal substring or regular expression (supports $1 backreferences).

chunkText.label: Chunk Text
chunkText.blurb: Split the input into fixed-size, optionally overlapping chunks — for feeding an LLM/embedding node piece by piece.

webFetch.label: Web Fetch
webFetch.blurb: Fetch a public URL and return its readable text (HTML stripped) — SSRF-guarded, no credential needed.

googleDrive.label: Google Drive
googleDrive.blurb: Search or read a file (as text) from your connected Google Drive.

iterator.label: Iterator
iterator.blurb: Forks the ONE node directly after it into a copy per array item (the input must be a JSON array, or '{"items":[...]}') — connect a Merge/Aggregator after that node to collect the results. Only a single processor step is forked; chain more after the aggregator.

analyzeImage.label: Analyze Image
analyzeImage.blurb: Vision analysis of an image URL — auto-routed to a vision-capable model.

extractDocumentData.label: Extract Document Data
extractDocumentData.blurb: Pull structured fields out of a document, invoice, or receipt image — vision analysis with a structured-extraction prompt, outputs JSON.

transcribeAudio.label: Transcribe Audio
transcribeAudio.blurb: Transcribe an audio file, or translate it directly to English — real Whisper API call (operator-configured, no per-tenant BYO key yet).

tutorials.catalogTitle: What do you want to learn?
tutorials.catalogLead: Choose a starting point. Your course is generated for your goals and experience, so no two learning paths need to be the same.
tutorials.customLead: From negotiation and public speaking to gardening, design, history, or a subject only you can name—Canvas can shape it into a course and match you with the right AI teacher.
tutorials.customPrompt: I want to learn a subject of my choice. First ask what I want to learn, why it matters to me, my current experience, preferred pace, and desired outcome. Then create a complete interactive LMS course object on the Canvas with modules, lessons, exercises, assessments, progress tracking, and a practical capstone. Create an appropriate specialist AI teacher agent, connect that agent to the course and Brain chat so the teacher joins the conversation, and begin teaching one step at a time. Adapt based on my answers and check my understanding. Do not only describe the course; create the course and teacher agent on the Canvas.
tutorials.coursePrompt: Create a complete interactive LMS course on the Canvas that teaches me {topic}. Focus the course on {focus}. Include structured modules, lessons, hands-on exercises, assessments, progress tracking, and a practical capstone. Create a specialist AI teacher agent named {agent}, give the agent expert teaching instructions for this subject, and connect the agent to both the course and Brain chat so the teacher joins our conversation. Begin by asking about my experience level and goal, then teach one step at a time, adapt to my answers, give useful feedback, and check my understanding. Do not only describe a curriculum; create the course object and teacher agent on the Canvas.

seo.title: About Builderforce.ai — One Operating System for Building and Running
seo.description: Meet Builderforce: the connected operating system where teams and AI agents create, operate, govern, and deliver from one shared context.

hero.title: Build the product. Run the company. One system.
hero.lead: Builderforce is the creative operating system for humans and AI agents—connecting the idea, the business, and the work that makes it real.
hero.visualAria: Builderforce operating system connecting product, finance, revenue, and governance

thesis.title: A company is a system. Its software should be one too.
thesis.body: Startups do not fail in neat departmental silos. A product decision changes runway. Customer feedback changes the roadmap. A security requirement changes delivery. Builderforce keeps those relationships visible, then gives people and agents a governed path from decision to action.

items.title: Create from intent
items.description: Turn an idea into connected websites, workflows, prototypes, datasets, models, plans, and products on one visual canvas.

items.title: Run on shared truth
items.description: Connect product, finance, revenue, customers, people, investors, marketing, and risk instead of rebuilding context in every tool.

items.title: Move decisions into action
items.description: Place specialist agents beside the work, review proposed changes, preserve evidence, and send approved work into delivery.

system.title: The whole operating picture, connected to execution
system.lead: Nine operating domains connect the company around one shared mission. Three foundations give every domain the same intelligence, business context, integrations, and governed Builderforce execution.

story.title: From IDEA to REAL.
story.bodyOne: Builderforce began with a simple belief: creating should not stop at the prototype. An idea becomes real only when the product, business context, people, and execution move together.
story.bodyTwo: Builderforce connects that entire journey in one shared workspace—from the first spark and customer signal to creative decisions, governed execution, and measurable outcomes.

principles.title: Principles for an agentic operating system

items.title: Startup-first
items.description: Every capability should help a team validate faster, conserve resources, earn revenue, reduce risk, or build something customers value.

items.title: Connected by default
items.description: Ideas, company data, decisions, artifacts, work, and outcomes should remain linked instead of becoming copies in another point tool.

items.title: Humans stay in the loop
items.description: Agents expand the team; they do not erase accountability. Review, approval, permissions, and clear ownership belong in the workflow.

items.title: Evidence over theater
items.description: Real objects, visible boundaries, retained execution records, and measurable outcomes matter more than an impressive but unverifiable answer.

trust.title: Governance is the work—not after it.
trust.body: Roles, approval paths, credential controls, audit history, privacy workflows, and system evidence are part of the platform architecture, giving teams a clearer route from experimentation to responsible operation.

cta.title: Bring your next idea—and the company behind it.
cta.body: Start on the canvas, connect the operating context, and give people and agents one place to turn intent into outcomes.

featuresPage.lede: Nine business domains, each owned by a C-suite teammate you can drag onto the board — so every capability maps to somebody accountable for it, not to a menu nobody owns.
featuresPage.domainsLede: Each domain is owned by a seat on your team. Open it from the menu or from the teammate — both land on the same surface, because both read the same list.
featuresPage.foundationsLede: Cross-cutting substrate. No single seat owns these — and notably, none of them is called “AI”: the model is the surface, not a department.
featuresPage.arcTitle: Idea to real, stage by stage
featuresPage.arcLede: The menu is not a list of departments. It is where you are in the journey, and every destination below sits in exactly one place.
featuresPage.arcNote: Generated from the product’s own navigation, so this table cannot advertise a destination that does not exist or miss one that does.

faq.a: There is one list now. The left panel groups destinations by where they sit in the arc — Idea, Make, Run — and the footer lists the people and agents who own them. Everything you used to reach from a sidebar is one of those two, and both read the same registry, so a name can never differ between them.

faq.q: Do I have to create a company to use this?
faq.a: No, and stopping partway is a complete, successful use of the product. Someone who ships three landing pages and never forms a company has not failed to onboard. The business rows stay listed the whole time — dim, not hidden — so you can see what is there before you need it.

Its destinations moved to the seats that own the work: expense categorisation to the CFO, contract analysis to Security, competitor monitoring to the CMO, pitch-deck feedback to the CEO. A menu item named after the technology is the tell that a product has not decided who the work belongs to.

faq.q: Why is a reference page a panel?
faq.a: Because losing your board to read about SOC 2 is a bad trade. Signed out these are ordinary pages with ordinary URLs. Signed in, the same page opens over the board you were working on, and Esc puts you back with your agent turn still running.

faq.q: Is the marketplace only for freelancers?
faq.a: No. Four families list side by side: talent, companies, agents and assets. Agents are not a separate area — buying one adds it to your team, which is why the catalogue and your roster can never drift apart.

featuresPage.closeLede: One platform instead of five, and one menu instead of seven. Start on the canvas; claim your company when you have one.
featuresPage.closeFine: No credit card · your board is yours before you sign up · upgrade whenever
