methodology.title: Idea to real
methodology.lede: Four stages say where you are. Three acts say what you do. The middle act is the whole opinion: reading an idea is cheap, building is not, and choosing which proof is worth running is the most consequential decision in the first month of anything.

read.title: Read
read.question: What did you actually say?
read.body: Paste an idea, a brief, an RFP or a contest — nothing needs cleaning up first. It comes back as a specification: what the thing has to do, which capabilities it names, and the limits the brief itself set. Reading writes nothing and builds nothing.
read.prompt: Read this idea and turn it into a specification — what it has to do, which capabilities it names, and the limits I have already set. Do not build anything yet. My idea:

prove.title: Prove
prove.question: Which question are you willing to spend money answering?
prove.body: Eight ways to make it real, ranked against your specification, cheapest first. Each leads with the question it answers and carries a kill condition — the number that would stop the project — set before it is built rather than after the result is in.
prove.prompt: Rank the ways to make this idea real, cheapest first. For each, tell me the question it answers and what it would cost. For the one you recommend, give me the kill condition — the number that would tell me to stop. My idea:

build.title: Build
build.question: Is it real, and where can I open it?
build.body: The chosen proof is materialised: files on the canvas, endpoints live, tickets on the board, the site published, and an address you can send to somebody. Agents pick the build tickets up from there.
build.prompt: Build the proof we settled on: write the files, stand up the endpoints, seed the tickets and publish it to an address I can send to somebody. What we are building:

methodology.arcNote: Measure is what makes this a loop rather than a line: the kill condition set during Prove is graded there, and the answer goes back to Idea. A proof with no condition that could fail is a launch with extra steps.
methodology.proofsHead: Eight ways to make it real
methodology.proofsLede: Ordered the way the product orders them — cheapest first. The recommendation never opens with the whole system, because the expensive failure is not building the wrong thing slowly. It is building the right-looking thing before finding out whether anyone wanted it.
methodology.proofsNote: Every option is always offered. This is advice about what to run first, not a filter — hiding an option would make it a verdict instead of a recommendation.

pitch.title: A method, not a feature list
pitch.body: The hardest objection in this category is “we already have AI tools”. The answer is not a longer feature list — it is that Builderforce sells a way of working: read the idea, choose the cheapest proof that answers the real question, then build it. Prospects who have been burned by a six-month build they never validated understand that sentence immediately, and it is the same sentence the product itself puts on screen.

identityProviders.clientSecretHint: Stored encrypted. It is never returned, so an empty value on save means “unchanged”.

identityProviders.issuerHint: The provider’s issuer URL, e.g. https://login.example.edu.
identityProviders.jitHint: Off means the provider authenticates somebody and we still refuse — for institutions that provision seats by hand.
identityProviders.keyGeneratedHint: A 2048-bit RSA signing key is generated and sealed when you save. Its public half is served at the JWKS URL above.
identityProviders.labelHint: What you will recognise this by later.
identityProviders.ltiSubtitle: The learning platforms allowed to launch a course into this workspace.

identityProviders.redirectUriHint: Register this exact value on the identity provider’s side. A mismatch fails with “redirect_uri_mismatch” and no further detail.
identityProviders.registrationIntro: Copy these from the LMS’s own tool configuration screen. We generate the signing key ourselves — you are never asked to paste a private key.

identityProviders.rotateKeyMessage: Launches from {label} keep working, but the platform caches our JWKS — ask their administrator to re-fetch it, or grade and roster calls will start failing with “invalid_client”.
identityProviders.samlNote: SAML 2.0 is terminated at an identity provider that already speaks it. Point a Shibboleth, InCommon or Entra IdP at an SSO gateway (WorkOS, Auth0, Okta, Entra) and connect that gateway here over OIDC — every signature verified in-process stays an RS256 token.
identityProviders.scopesHint: Must include `openid`, or the provider returns nothing to verify.
identityProviders.ssoSubtitle: Let an institution’s own identity provider authenticate its people into this workspace.
identityProviders.toolUrlsHint: Paste these into the LMS’s tool configuration. Every one must match this deployment exactly.

gradedProofRate.label: Ideas reaching a graded proof
gradedProofRate.definition: Ideas whose proof had its kill condition measured. A deliverable nobody graded does not qualify.

timeToProofChoice.label: Time to a chosen proof form
timeToProofChoice.definition: First prompt to the moment a proof form was chosen. Measures the decision, not the build.

readBeforeBuildRate.label: Ideas that Read before they Build
readBeforeBuildRate.definition: Of ideas that started a build, those whose idea was read and its proofs ranked first. Not measured until something is built.

timeToArtifact.label: Time to first meaningful artifact
timeToArtifact.definition: First prompt to the first non-chat artifact on the board.

reachableProofRate.label: Proofs reaching a real, reachable artifact
reachableProofRate.definition: Build attempts that produced an address a person can open. A built proof with no address does not qualify.

deliverableRate.label: Sessions reaching a real deliverable
deliverableRate.definition: A successful publish, project handoff or workflow execution. A draft canvas object does not qualify.

validationRate.label: Artifact validation pass rate
validationRate.definition: Validations that passed. Proof grading is excluded — a missed kill condition is a finding, not a defect.

deliveryRetryRate.label: Delivery retry rate
deliveryRetryRate.definition: Failed attempts that were followed by another attempt, over attempts.

proofGradingRate.label: Proofs whose kill condition was graded
proofGradingRate.definition: Built proofs that got a measured verdict. The one metric separating this method from a launch with extra steps.

collaborationRate.label: Sessions inviting a human or agent
collaborationRate.definition: Sessions with a second member or at least one contributing agent.

agentParticipation.label: Agent group-chat participation
agentParticipation.definition: Distinct agents that contributed a turn. Counted only where agents took part at all.

synthesisRate.label: Successful agent synthesis
synthesisRate.definition: Group sessions closed by an explicit Brain synthesis after the agent turns. Message volume alone does not qualify.

resumed7d.label: Sessions resumed within 7 days
resumed7d.definition: Reopened more than an hour after creation and inside 7 days. Only sessions old enough to have had the chance count.

resumed30d.label: Sessions resumed within 30 days
resumed30d.definition: Reopened more than an hour after creation and inside 30 days. Only sessions old enough to have had the chance count.

outputReuse.label: Created outputs reused as inputs
outputReuse.definition: Reuse events — a created output fed back in as the input to something else.

humanIntervention.label: Human interventions per delivery
humanIntervention.definition: Approvals, revisions and retries a person performed, per successful delivery. Lower is better only while quality holds.

costPerDelivery.label: Cost per delivered outcome
costPerDelivery.definition: Attributed cost per successful delivery. Not measured until authoritative cost telemetry is attached.

latencyPerDelivery.label: Latency per delivered outcome
latencyPerDelivery.definition: Mean wall-clock duration of a successful delivery. Not measured until durations are recorded.

correlationCoverage.label: Actions with a correlated outcome
correlationCoverage.definition: Terminal events that have a matching started event. A feature is not fully instrumented below 100%.
